_about: Where each case rule must fire (true positive) and where it must stay silent (false-positive check). Counts are per capture run. 'exactly' when the number is fully explained by the evidence, 'at_least' when it depends on replay timing. Checked by scripts/test_detections.py against the latest run of each capture.

rules.name: Lumma-style browser fingerprint upload
rules.why: two fingerprint POSTs in case 1: Chrome at 23:05:40 and Edge at 23:05:47

rules.name: Upload-heavy TLS session to an outside host
rules.why: three uploads to the Lumma C2: 253 KB, 388 KB, 1.42 MB

rules.name: Burst of LSA name lookups (domain group discovery)
rules.why: 748 lookups in 3 s; the rule fires once, then stays quiet for 60 s (ignore=60)

rules.name: KongTuke-style backdoor HTTP C2 path (& + 64-hex token)
rules.why: 99 HTTP requests of the implant (69 to the main C2, 30 to the fallback servers) all use the layout

rules.name: Large plain-HTTP upload (POST >= 1 MB to an outside host)
HTTP polling: 20+ empty (204) replies from one host in 5 min
rules.why: 52 empty replies from the C2; ignore=300 limits repeats

rules.name: Same name fails to resolve 10+ times in 5 min (dead C2 fallback)
rules.why: three dead fallback domains, 15-16 failures each; ignore=300 applies to the whole rule, so the first one fires

rules.name: Non-TLS traffic to TCP 443 (protocol detection failed)
rules.why: one 37-minute RAT connection to its server on 443; flowbits limit the rule to one alert per connection

rules.name: Command-line tool downloads a Windows program over HTTP
rules.why: curl/8.21.0 fetched runner_ilove.exe from a bare IP on port 9000

rules.name: Command-line HTTP request from a workstation (visibility)
rules.why: the two curl script fetches from holtandberyl; the program download goes to 100840 instead

rules.name: DNS-over-HTTPS from a client
rules.why: one TLS session to dns.google right before the C2 connection
